title: A Transformer-Based Framework for Multimodal Learning
excerpt: We present a unified transformer architecture that jointly encodes text, images and tabular signals. By sharing a cross-modal attention backbone and introducing modality-specific adapters, the framework improves accuracy on five multimodal benchmarks while reducing parameter count by 38% compared to late-fusion baselines.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Scientific Question Answering
excerpt: Large language models often hallucinate when answering domain-specific scientific questions. We introduce a retrieval-augmented reasoning pipeline that grounds each reasoning step in cited passages, improving factual accuracy by 21 points on SciQA while producing verifiable evidence chains.
content: Large language models often hallucinate when answering domain-specific scientific questions. title: Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training with Sparse Attention
excerpt: We propose a block-sparse attention pattern that scales sub-quadratically with sequence length. Combined with a curriculum over context lengths, it trains 1.8× faster than dense attention on 64k-token documents with no loss in downstream quality.

title: Fairness-Aware Feature Selection for Public Sector Data
excerpt: Public-sector predictive models must balance accuracy with equitable outcomes. We formulate feature selection as a constrained optimisation problem that bounds disparate impact, and evaluate it on three government datasets with domain experts.

title: Explainable AI for Healthcare Decision Support
excerpt: Clinicians are reluctant to adopt black-box models. We develop a case-based explanation method that surfaces similar historical patients alongside counterfactual feature changes, and show in a user study with 42 clinicians that it increases appropriate trust without reducing accuracy.

title: A Survey on Deep Learning for Natural Language Processing
excerpt: This survey reviews a decade of deep learning methods for NLP — from word embeddings and recurrent networks to pre-trained transformers — and organises open challenges around robustness, efficiency and evaluation.

title: Probabilistic Graph Models for Student Performance Prediction
excerpt: We model course prerequisite structures as probabilistic graphs to forecast student outcomes early in a term, enabling targeted interventions. The approach outperforms gradient-boosted baselines on data from 11,000 students.

title: Low-Resource Machine Translation via Cross-Lingual Transfer
excerpt: We study transfer from high-resource language pairs to Bengali, Swahili and Nepali, showing that script-aware subword sharing yields consistent BLEU gains of 3–6 points over strong multilingual baselines.

title: Interpretable Ensembles through Rule Distillation
excerpt: We distil tree ensembles into compact rule lists that retain 97% of ensemble accuracy while remaining human-readable, and provide generalisation bounds for the distilled models.
